steps: Give IV HYDROCORTISONE 100 mg immediately — do NOT wait for cortisol results.
Aggressive IV fluids (0.9% saline) to correct volume and hypotension.
Treat the precipitant (often infection); continue hydrocortisone (e.g. 50 mg q6h) then taper.
Sick-day rules and steroid-emergency card education on recovery.

drugRefs.route: IV bolus (IM if no IV access)
drugRefs.why: Life-saving glucocorticoid replacement — give on clinical suspicion without waiting for cortisol/ACTH results.

drugRefs.dose: ~1 L over the first hour, then titrated to volume status
drugRefs.why: Corrects hypovolaemia and hypotension from cortisol/aldosterone deficiency.
Glucocorticoid deficiency causes hypoglycaemia; correct alongside electrolyte disturbance.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Adrenal Insufficiency and Crisis
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Primary Adrenal Insufficiency
Society for Endocrinology Emergency Guidance — Acute Adrenal Insufficiency

drugRefs.duration: until stable, then taper to oral replacement
drugRefs.why: Continues cover after the initial bolus while the precipitant (often infection) is treated; a continuous infusion (~200 mg/24 h) is an alternative. Taper as the patient recovers.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Adrenal Insufficiency and Crisis
Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline — Primary Adrenal Insufficiency

confirm: Hypotension/shock, vomiting, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia ± known adrenal insufficiency or steroid withdrawal/stress. Treat on suspicion.
